answer: Treat identity like a terrace: each hillside holds a fixed number of plots, and a new key must claim a free one by lashing ongoing signed work onto a shared trellis. A randomness beacon drawn from the nebula of recent blocks picks which plots are cross-audited each epoch, so a farm cannot stack thousands of keys on one slab. Because plots are capped and every key must carry fresh verified work or be reaped, cloning stays costly. Cost: scarce plots plus real labor per key, and idle keys decay. The nebula seeds each audit; the trellis holds the work; the terrace stays scarce.
